There is no single best AI music video generator. There are a few very different jobs people mean by "AI music video", and each tool on this list is built for one of them. Pick the job first, then the tool.

The short answer:

  • You have a finished song and want visuals that move with it: Neural Frames or Freebeat.
  • You want stylized, animated art for a track: Kaiber.
  • You want cinematic shots and will edit them together yourself: Runway.
  • You want a rap video of you and a friend, song included, from two photos: Rap Duo AI.

What to check before you pick one

  • Does it use your audio? Some tools build the video around a song you upload. Others write the music too. If you already have a track, you need the first kind.
  • Who is on screen? Most music video tools make abstract or stylized visuals, or characters from a prompt. Very few put specific real people, from their photos, on screen performing.
  • How much editing? Some give you a finished video in one go; others give you clips to cut together.
  • Format: vertical 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, or 16:9 for YouTube.

Features and prices change often. Check each tool's own site for current plans before you buy.

Neural Frames: visuals that react to your song

Neural Frames is built for musicians with a finished track. It can split a song into stems (drums, bass, vocals and so on) and let each one drive the visuals, so a kick drum can trigger a cut or a colour change. It is the pick when the music comes first and you want the picture to follow it closely.

Not for: putting you or your friends on screen as performers.

Freebeat: the fastest beat-synced clip

Freebeat analyses a song's tempo and energy and generates visuals that hit the beat, with little setup. It suits creators who post often and want a clip per song without editing.

Not for: a specific person performing, or a long, story-driven video.

Kaiber: stylized, animated music art

Kaiber turns images and prompts into animated video in a chosen look (painterly, anime, surreal) and can sync the motion to uploaded audio. It is a favourite for visualizers and lyric-style videos where the style is the point.

Not for: a realistic video of real people rapping or singing.

Runway: cinematic shots, edited by you

Runway is a general AI video studio: you describe or show the shot and it generates it, with editing tools alongside. Indie artists use it to build cinematic music videos shot by shot. Expect to spend time directing and cutting.

Not for: a one-tap finished video.

Rap Duo AI: a rap video starring you and a friend

This is ours, and it does one narrow thing. Add a photo of each person (or one photo of the two of you), pick a stage, optionally type what the rap is about, and it writes an original rap and beat and renders the two of you performing it, lip-synced, in about 2 to 3 minutes. It is the tool behind the viral Hotel Lobby AI trend, the orange-booth duo videos.

  • Output: vertical 9:16 by default, a standard song is 12 seconds at 720p, with higher resolutions and longer lengths on the better models.
  • Languages: the rap follows the language you write the topic in (English, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese and more).
  • Price: one song is $9.99, packs start at $29 for 5 songs, and the Basic plan is 10 songs a month for $29.90. A render that fails is never charged.

Not for: your own song or your own recorded vocals (it writes and performs its own rap), cloning a real artist's voice, or more than two performers.

See it step by step in how to make an AI rap video, or go straight to the AI music video generator.

Which one should you use?

  • "I made a song and need a video for Spotify Canvas, YouTube or TikTok." Neural Frames if you want the visuals to follow every part of the track, Freebeat if you want it fast.
  • "I want an artsy visualizer." Kaiber.
  • "I'm directing a proper music video." Runway, and plan for editing time.
  • "I want a funny or sweet rap video with my friend, partner or sibling." Rap Duo AI. It is also what people use for birthday rap songs and funny birthday videos.

FAQ

Is there a free AI music video generator? Most of these tools have a free tier or a free first try with limits (watermarks, lower resolution, a few credits). Full-quality, watermark-free videos are paid almost everywhere.

Can an AI music video generator use my own song? Neural Frames, Freebeat and Kaiber build video around audio you upload. Runway generates the picture and you add your audio in the edit. Rap Duo AI does not use uploaded audio: it writes and performs an original rap.

Can AI make a music video of me? Rap Duo AI puts two real people from their photos into a rap performance. The other tools here focus on stylized visuals or prompt-made characters rather than a specific person performing.

Which is best for TikTok and Reels? Any tool that exports vertical 9:16. Freebeat and Rap Duo AI give finished vertical videos without editing.

  • Rap lyrics (text): AI chat assistants like ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, or a dedicated lyrics tool.
  • A rap song (audio with vocals and a beat): Suno or Udio.
  • A rap video of real people performing: Rap Duo AI, for two people from two photos.

Pick the output first, then the tool.

AI rap lyrics generators

If you plan to rap it yourself, you only need words. Any capable AI chat assistant writes decent verses if you are specific: the topic, the mood, a rhyme scheme (AABB, ABAB), bars per verse, and a reference style ("laid-back, West Coast"). Ask for a hook separately and for internal rhymes if the first draft is flat.

Where they stop: it's text. The flow, the beat and the performance are still on you.

AI rap song generators: Suno and Udio

Suno and Udio turn a prompt into a full song with vocals and a beat, and rap is one of the styles they handle. You can let them write the lyrics or paste your own. They are the pick when you want audio: a track to share, a demo, a joke song for the group chat.

Where they stop: there's no video of anyone performing, and the voice isn't yours. Check each service's terms for commercial use before you release anything.

An AI rap video of you and a friend: Rap Duo AI

This is ours, and it does one thing: add a photo of each of two people (or one photo of both), write a topic of up to 120 characters, pick a stage, and it writes an original rap and beat and renders the two of you performing it, lip-synced, in about 2 to 3 minutes. It is what people use for the Hotel Lobby AI trend, birthday rap songs and rap battles.

Where it stops: it works from a topic, not your full lyrics; it doesn't use uploaded audio or clone anyone's voice; and it's made for two performers. Full videos are paid with credits (one song $9.99, plans from $29.90 a month); a render that fails is never charged.

Try it on the AI rap generator page, or read how to make an AI rap video step by step.

How to get better AI raps, whatever the tool

  • Be specific. "Maya turns 25 and still can't wake up before noon" beats "a birthday rap".
  • Name the vibe. Hype, laid-back, old school, drill, a roast.
  • One idea per verse. AI raps wander when the prompt tries to cover everything.
  • Keep it yours. Don't ask for a real artist's lyrics or voice; ask for a style instead.

FAQ

What is the best free AI rap generator? For lyrics, most AI chat assistants write raps on their free tiers. Song and video generators usually give a limited free try and charge for full-quality results.

Can AI make a rap song with my voice? Some tools offer voice cloning of your own voice. Rap Duo AI doesn't clone voices; it performs an original rap with generated vocals.

Can AI rap in Spanish or other languages? Yes. Chat assistants and song generators handle many languages, and Rap Duo AI raps in the language you write the topic in.

Which AI rap generator makes a video? Rap Duo AI renders a music video of two real people from their photos. Song generators like Suno and Udio produce audio only.

What makes them work

The rapper and the DJ. Eric B. & Rakim, Gang Starr and Pete Rock & CL Smooth are the classic setup: one voice, one producer, one sound you can recognize in two bars. Rakim's calm, internal-rhyme flow over Eric B.'s beats changed how people rapped.

The two voices that trade. OutKast, UGK, Mobb Deep, Clipse and Run the Jewels are two rappers who pass the mic back and forth. OutKast's Speakerboxxx/The Love Below won the Grammy for Album of the Year in 2004, still one of the few rap albums to do it.

The brothers. Clipse (Pusha T and Malice) and Rae Sremmurd (Swae Lee and Slim Jxmmi) are brothers, and it shows in how tight the back-and-forth is. "Black Beatles" went to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2016.

The firsts. DJ Jazzy Jeff & The Fresh Prince won the first Grammy ever given for a rap performance, for "Parents Just Don't Understand" (1989 ceremony). Kris Kross's "Jump" spent eight weeks at No. 1 in 1992.

Honorable mention: Unc & Phew

Quavo and Takeoff of Migos, uncle and nephew, recorded as the duo Unc & Phew in 2022. Their single "Hotel Lobby (Unc & Phew)" and its orange-booth performance became the Hotel Lobby AI trend in 2026. The full story is in Quavo and Takeoff: Unc & Phew explained.

Every duo above started with two people and a mic. You can put yourself and a friend, a partner or a sibling in a rap duo video from two photos: the Rap Duo AI studio writes an original rap and beat about whatever you choose and renders the two of you performing it, lip-synced, in about 3 minutes. It doesn't use any real artist's song or clone anyone's voice.

For songs about the friendship itself, see rap songs about friends. Need a name first? Try the rap duo name generator. Want the viral look? Pick the orange booth on the Hotel Lobby AI page, or see how to make an AI rap video step by step.

FAQ

Who is the best rap duo of all time? OutKast is the most common answer: a string of classic albums, a Grammy Album of the Year and two very different voices that fit. Eric B. & Rakim, UGK and Mobb Deep are the usual picks right behind them.

What are some female rap duos? City Girls (Yung Miami and JT) from Miami are the best-known female rap duo of recent years, with hits like "Act Up" (2018).

What is a rap duet? A song where two rappers share the track, trading verses or lines. Rap duos make them by default; a duet can also be a one-off between solo artists.

Are rap duos still a thing? Yes: Run the Jewels and Rae Sremmurd kept the format alive in the 2010s, and the Hotel Lobby trend turned "two people, one mic" into something anyone can do.

Here are 18 original, clean bars about everyday life, the funny rap songs that do it best, and how to turn your own into a video.

Home life

Food

How to write a funny rap

A lot of the Hotel Lobby AI videos on TikTok, Reels and LinkedIn were made on Higgsfield, an AI video platform with many models and tools. If you searched for "Higgsfield Hotel Lobby", here's how creators say they do it, what that involves, and a simpler route if all you want is two people rapping in the orange booth.

Higgsfield changes its interface often. The steps below are what creators described in their own tutorials in late September 2026, not official Higgsfield instructions; check the app for the current version.

How people make the Hotel Lobby video on Higgsfield

Creator tutorials describe two ways, both inside Higgsfield's Genjutsu tool, which recasts a video with your own character:

1. Recreate a community template.

  1. Sign up for Higgsfield (some tutorials mention a paid Pro account).
  2. Open the Genjutsu tab and browse the community video library for a Hotel Lobby video.
  3. Click Recreate, remove the reference photos and upload your own.
  4. Keep the prompt that came with it and tap Generate. It takes a few minutes.

2. Motion transfer from the original clip.

  1. In Genjutsu, choose the Motion Transfer model.
  2. Upload the original Hotel Lobby performance as the video reference.
  3. Upload your photo and generate.

Either way, the result follows the original COLORS performance: the original moves, framing and timing, with your face recast into it. Higgsfield is credit-based; how many credits a video takes depends on the model and length, so check its pricing page before you start.

What that involves

Higgsfield is a powerful general-purpose tool, and if you want full control over the original clip it's a good choice. For the Hotel Lobby trend specifically, a few things trip people up:

  • Finding the right template or clip. Community templates come and go, and motion transfer needs you to get the original video first.
  • One face at a time. Many tutorials recast one person. Getting you and a friend into the booth takes more steps.
  • The original song. A recast of the original clip keeps Quavo and Takeoff's copyrighted track, and videos using it can be muted or taken down on some platforms.
  • An account and a plan before your first video.

The simpler way: two photos, one tap

If what you want is two real people in the orange booth, a photo-to-video maker built for exactly this is quicker:

  1. Add one photo of each person, or one photo of the two of you together. Clear, front-facing, good light.
  2. Write who it's for in one line: "Jake's 30th birthday", "best friends since 2nd grade", "our salon's grand opening". The rap is written around it.
  3. Tap once. Both of you appear in a Hotel Lobby-style orange booth, trading verses on an original song and beat, ready in about 3 minutes.

No template to hunt for, no reference clip, no prompt to write. It runs in the browser on iPhone, Android or desktop. The song is original, so there's no copyrighted track for platforms to flag. One song is $9.99, packs start at $29 for 5 songs, and a render that fails is never charged.

Before it was an AI trend, "Hotel Lobby" was a song, and before it was a meme, it was one of the last performances Quavo and Takeoff made together. Here's the story behind the orange booth everyone is putting themselves into.

Who made "Hotel Lobby"?

"Hotel Lobby (Unc & Phew)" is by Quavo and Takeoff, two of the three members of Migos. Quavo is Takeoff's uncle, which is where the duo name comes from: Unc & Phew, uncle and nephew. That's also why people search for it as "Migos Hotel Lobby" and why the trend is sometimes called the Migos AI trend, even though Offset isn't on the song. (More on the two of them in Quavo and Takeoff: Unc & Phew explained.)

  • Released: May 20, 2022, as the first single from their joint album Only Built for Infinity Links
  • Producers: Murda Beatz, Keanu Beats and Fabio Aguilar
  • Charts: No. 55 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 12 on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs
  • Certifications: Platinum in the US, Gold in Brazil and France, Silver in the UK

The official music video, directed by Keemotion and Quavo, is a nod to the film Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas, with the two in the desert and in a Las Vegas hotel.

The A COLORS SHOW performance

The version the trend copies isn't the music video. It's the A COLORS SHOW performance released in June 2022, about a month after the single: Quavo and Takeoff side by side in front of a bright orange backdrop, trading verses into two microphones. It has passed 100 million views on YouTube, and that orange room is now one of the most recognizable sets on the internet.

What is "Hotel Lobby" about?

It's a back-and-forth flex record. The two trade verses about success, money and the life they built together, and the chemistry of uncle and nephew finishing each other's lines is the point. That easy two-person energy is exactly what makes it work as a duo trend.

Takeoff

Takeoff was killed in Houston in November 2022, only months after the COLORS video. In June 2023, Quavo and Offset performed "Hotel Lobby" together at the BET Awards as a tribute to him. For many fans the COLORS clip is a way to remember him, which is why some feel uneasy seeing it turned into an AI gag.

How the Hotel Lobby AI trend started

In early September 2026 a clip of two cats "performing" Hotel Lobby took off on TikTok. Within days, AI face-swap versions followed: former presidents, Breaking Bad's Walter White and Jesse Pinkman, athletes, superheroes, pets and, mostly, ordinary friends and couples. On September 23, 2026, Quavo reposted the original COLORS performance on X, pointing the new audience back to where it started.

Make your own, respectfully

The kindest version of the trend is the one with you in it: you and your best friend, your partner or your sibling, not the original artists. Good rap battle lines are specific, they rhyme on the last word, and they land the joke at the end of the second line. Here are 25 original, clean roast bars grouped by the kind of friend you're battling, then how to write your own and turn the battle into a video.

The late one

You're always late, it's a fact, not a rumor,
your watch runs on vibes and a bad sense of humor.

You showed up at ten for a party at eight,
even your excuses are running late.

The bad cook

Your cooking's so bad that the smoke alarm cheers,
the only applause that you've gotten in years.

You burned a salad, I'm still in shock,
you'd need a recipe to boil a rock.

The gym member who never goes

You've got a gym membership framed on the wall,
the only thing there that got lifted at all.

You say you're bulking, I say you're just eating,
your only PR is the snooze you're repeating.

The gamer

You rage-quit so fast the controller's in therapy,
your K/D's so low it's practically charity.

You camp in the corner and call it a strategy,
your aim is so off it should come with an apology.

The group chat ghost

You leave me on read like it's part of your brand,
three days for a "k", I don't understand.

Your voice notes are podcasts, eleven minutes long,
to tell me the pizza you ordered was wrong.

The fashion risk

You wear Crocs with socks and you call it a flex,
the fashion police got your photo on their desk.

Sunglasses indoors and your hat to the side,
you look like a GPS that lost its guide.

The driver

You drive like a GPS stuck on "recalculate",
four left turns just to find the front gate.

You parked in two spaces, and one was a lawn,
the HOA wrote you a letter at dawn.

The "rapper"

Your flow is so slow it's stuck on buffering mode,
your rhymes need a map and a ZIP code.

You rap like a ringtone from 2009,
stuck on one beat and you're still off time.

You call yourself fire, but I'm feeling a chill,
your bars are so weak they need a doctor's bill.

The cheap one

You split the free samples, then asked me to tip,
you'd Venmo-request me for one little sip.

The selfie addict

Ninety-nine selfies to post just the one,
your camera's exhausted, your front flash is done.

The sleeper

You sleep until noon and call it "early to rise",
your alarm clock quit for a new job, surprise.

The sibling

Mom's favorite? Please, that's a story you tell,
she only says it so you'll clean up as well.

The coworker

You reply-all to everyone, up to the CEO,
to say thanks for a meeting that ended an hour ago.

You're on mute every call, then you talk for a while,
we've been reading your lips, silent-movie style.

The sports fan

Your team hasn't won since your dad still had hair,
you still wear the jersey like somebody cares.

The dancer

You dance like a phone on a table, vibrating,
the DJ stopped the song and he's still hesitating.

How to write your own roast bars

  1. Pick one real detail. The burned salad, the 3 days on read, the lawn parking. One detail your friend will recognize beats ten generic insults.
  2. Put the punchline last. Set it up in the first line, land it on the last word of the second.
  3. Rhyme the ends. "Rumor / humor", "therapy / charity": the rhyme is what makes it sound like a bar and not a complaint.
  4. Keep it a roast. Aim at habits, not at things people can't change, and only battle people who are in on the joke.
